name: Xie Zhigang
current_role: Legal representative, Hunan Yuteng Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd. (per third-party business registry; not confirmed by official source)
profile: Xie Zhigang (谢志刚) appeared on the Hurun China list in 2010 for 'Yuteng Chemical Industrial' (electrolytic lead, silver, lead oxide). A third-party registry lists a Xie Zhigang as legal representative of Hunan Yuteng Nonferrous Metals, founded 2001 in Chenzhou, which produces electrolytic lead plus gold, silver, antimony and bismuth by-products. Link is plausible but not officially confirmed.
interesting_fact: Hunan Yuteng reports capacity of ~100,000 t/yr of electrolytic lead and ~2,000 t/yr of silver; its lead and silver are registered on the Shanghai Futures Exchange, LME and LBMA, and it hosted the 14th China Lead & Zinc Summit in 2019.
notes: Very low public profile; only on Hurun 2010. Identity link to Hunan Yuteng is from a 36Kr registry page (third-party). Company website listed there may be the only route; verify via China's national enterprise credit system before outreach.

name: Nitin Raojibhai Desai
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Desai Brothers Ltd (Pune); Independent Director, Zydus Lifesciences
profile: Pune industrialist who heads Desai Brothers, a family group founded in Gujarat in 1901 that is one of India's largest bidi makers and diversified into food (Mother's Recipe pickles, acquired 2002), finance, hospitality and renewable energy. He has been an independent director of Zydus Lifesciences since 2011 and was on the Force Motors board 2014-2022.
interesting_fact: The Desai group traces back to 1901 in Gujarat, still makes about 70 million bidis a day, and bought the 'Mother's Recipe' pickle brand in 2002 for roughly Rs 6 crore before demerging food into Desai Foods in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He is a civil engineer with a master's in environmental engineering from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, and chairs The Poona Blind Men's Association; he was also President of Poona Club.
notes: Private family group; no published personal/office email found. Group's renewable-energy arm is a possible angle for the energy podcast. Route via Desai Brothers corporate office or Zydus company secretary.

name: SV Balasubramaniam
current_role: Chairman, Bannari Amman Sugars Ltd and founder-chairman, Bannari Amman Group (Coimbatore)
profile: Dr. S.V. Balasubramaniam, a chartered accountant and company secretary from Sangampalayam village near Coimbatore, founded the Bannari Amman Group, which grew from sugar in the early 1980s into distilleries, granite, wind power and education. The board re-appointed him as chairman of listed Bannari Amman Sugars in 2025.
interesting_fact: Bannari Amman Group started Tamil Nadu's first biodiesel plant (2007) and runs wind power alongside its sugar, alcohol and granite businesses, using molasses from sugar production for its distilleries.
deep_cut_fact: He hails from Sangampalayam village near Coimbatore and trained as both a chartered accountant and a company secretary before building the group; he also founded the Bannari Amman Institute of Technology in Sathyamangalam.
notes: Elderly founder; son B. Saravanan is MD. Energy angle: wind power, cogeneration, ethanol/biodiesel. Company secretary C. Palaniswamy signs filings; secretary@bannari.com also published in BRSR report.

name: Liu Xingxu
current_role: Chairman, China XLX Fertiliser Ltd (HKEX: 1866) / Xinlianxin Chemical Industry Group
profile: Liu Xingxu (刘兴旭), about 71, has led Henan-based XLX (心连心), one of China's largest urea and compound-fertiliser makers, for over 30 years; he became executive director when it listed (Singapore, later Hong Kong). His holding vehicle Pioneer Top Holdings repeatedly increased its stake in 2026 to ~32.7%.
interesting_fact: In September 2026 he launched XLX's high-end nitro (nitrate-based) fertiliser line, pitching it as the start of an 'activated nitro-fertiliser era' for Chinese agriculture.
deep_cut_fact: He is senior vice-chairman of the China Nitrogen Fertilizer Industry Association, with more than 30 years in the fertiliser industry.

public_contacts.value: PRChina Limited - David Shiu dshiu@prchina.com.hk / Liky Guo lguo@prchina.com.hk (investor & media contacts)

notes: Energy angle: coal-based ammonia/urea and energy-efficiency. Best route is the IR agency PRChina.

name: Shi Jian
current_role: Former chairman of SRE Group (Shanghai real estate, HKEX: 1207); left the SRE board in 2015; current role unknown
profile: Shi Jian co-founded SRE Group (上置集团) with Si Xiaodong in the early 1990s; it became a major Shanghai residential developer listed in Hong Kong, and he was also chairman of China New Town Development from 2010. He appeared on Hurun China lists 2001-2008. He has been out of public view since stepping down from SRE in 2015.
interesting_fact: SRE's Shanghai projects included the 'Oasis Albany Garden' (上置·绿洲雅宾利花园) in Zhabei district, later sold to a Vanke subsidiary in 2015.
notes: Chinese name in source list (施健) differs from that used in Chinese press (施建). In 2015 PRC authorities required him to remain in China and HKEX later found listing-rule breaches (HKEX 2018 notice) - avoid as an outreach target unless current status is confirmed. No public contact.

name: Anil Sarin
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, TARC Limited (formerly Anant Raj Global), New Delhi
profile: Anil Sarin is a co-founder of the Delhi-based Anant Raj real-estate group (with brother Ashok Sarin) and was its managing director until 2020. Since 2016 he has chaired TARC Ltd, the luxury residential developer demerged from Anant Raj; he was re-appointed chairman in May 2024. Anant Raj itself has pivoted into data centres, targeting ~307 MW by FY32.
interesting_fact: Anant Raj, the group he co-founded, plans to invest about US$2.1 billion to scale its data-centre capacity from 28 MW to ~307 MW by FY32, carving the business into Ashok Cloud Pvt Ltd.
notes: For data-center angle, Anant Raj MD Amit Sarin is the public face. TARC IR: Ankush Vijan (no email published). Data aggregators conflict on dates of his Anant Raj roles.

name: Aristeidis J Pittas
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Euroseas Ltd (NASDAQ: ESEA), EuroDry Ltd (NASDAQ: EDRY) and Euroholdings
profile: Greek shipowner Aristides Pittas co-founded ship manager Eurobulk with his brothers in 1995, founded containership owner Euroseas in 2005 (NASDAQ IPO 2007) and spun off drybulk owner EuroDry in 2018; he has also chaired Euroholdings since 2024. The Pittas family controls the companies.
interesting_fact: He holds a BSc in Marine Engineering from Newcastle University and a double master's from MIT in Ocean Systems Management and Naval Architecture & Marine Engineering.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Eurobulk he worked at Elefsina Shipyards, at Varnima (Vardinoyannis Group) and at Petros Pappas' Oceanbulk; he is treasurer of marine-environment group HELMEPA and was president of the Athens College alumni association (SAKA) 2021-2024.

public_contacts.value: Capital Link Inc. (Nicolas Bornozis / Markella Kara) - euroseas@capitallink.com

notes: Regular speaker at Capital Link shipping forums - a natural outreach channel. Energy angle: shipping decarbonisation/HELMEPA.

name: Jeff Horing
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Director, Insight Partners; Chair of monday.com board; director of nCino
profile: Jeff Horing co-founded Insight Partners (originally Insight Venture Partners) with Jerry Murdock in 1995 after stints at Warburg Pincus and Goldman Sachs; it became one of the largest software-focused growth/VC firms. He leads its investment team and sits on boards including monday.com (chair) and nCino.
interesting_fact: In Insight's early days, Horing and Murdock sourced every deal themselves by scanning software trade publications for companies that were hiring; he says 'Sourcing is everything' and calls analysts the 'lifeblood of Insight'.
deep_cut_fact: He has said Insight's bottom-up, data-driven sourcing model was inspired by Summit Partners and TA Associates; he likens investing to baseball - an investor's edge comes only from the pitches they actually see.
notes: Described by Fortune as low-profile. Route via Insight Partners press/communications team (insightpartners.com). He was a guest on Invest Like the Best EP.440 (https://podwise.ai/episodes/5210842) - useful prep.

name: Zhou Weibin
current_role: Unknown (listed by Hurun China 2001-2006 as owner of Goldencrown Group, coatings)
profile: Zhou Weibin (周伟彬) appeared on Hurun China rich lists from 2001 to 2006 with an estimated fortune of ~US$100m from Goldencrown Group, a Chinese coatings/paint maker. No current public information confirming his role or the company's status could be found in English or Chinese sources.
notes: Could not verify identity or current activity; Goldencrown (金冠) coatings link not found online. Check China's National Enterprise Credit Information system before any outreach.

name: Gregg C Sengstack
current_role: Retired Executive Chairperson, Franklin Electric (retired 2025); Director, Woodward Inc. and Allegion plc
profile: Gregg Sengstack spent ~37 years at Franklin Electric (pumps, water and fueling systems), joining in 1988 as assistant treasurer, becoming CFO in 1999, CEO 2014-2024 and chair from 2015; he expanded its energy systems, water-treatment and U.S. distribution businesses. He retired in 2025 and remains on the boards of Woodward (energy conversion/aerospace) and Allegion.
interesting_fact: He rose from assistant treasurer to CEO at the same company, leading Franklin Electric's push into fueling systems, water treatment and connected (IoT) pumping solutions.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Franklin Electric he headed its Franklin Fueling Systems and International Water businesses; he holds a bachelor's from Bucknell University and an MBA from the University of Chicago.
notes: Retired from Franklin Electric in 2025 (Retirement & Consulting Agreement in SEC filing). No personal channels found; reach via Woodward or Allegion corporate secretary. Relevant for energy/fueling/water infrastructure angle.

name: John Belizaire
current_role: CEO and Director, Soluna Holdings (NASDAQ: SLNH)
profile: Serial software entrepreneur (founded Theory Center, sold to BEA Systems, and FirstBest Systems, sold to Guidewire) and former Intel architect, Belizaire co-founded Soluna Computing, which builds data centers co-located with wind and solar farms to use curtailed renewable power. Soluna merged into Mechanical Technology Inc. in 2021 and he became CEO of Soluna Holdings in 2023, now pivoting to AI/HPC hosting.
interesting_fact: Soluna's flagship wind-powered West Texas campus, Project Dorothy, is named after Dorothy Vaughan, one of NASA's 'Human Computers', and soaks up curtailed power from a 150 MW wind farm.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his first company he was lead architect for Intel's Digital Enterprise Group; he holds a BS and MEng in Computer Science from Cornell.

public_contacts.value: hello@soluna.io (listed for Investor Relations and Media, 2024)
West of Fairfax (PR agency named on Soluna press releases)

notes: Ideal guest for energy + data-center podcast; frequent podcast guest and speaker (e.g. Bigger Than Us #184, Through The Noise). Very approachable via Soluna PR.

name: Greg Warnock
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Director, Mercato Partners (Salt Lake City); board member at MNTN (formerly SteelHouse)
profile: Utah venture investor who co-founded early-stage fund vSpring Capital and then growth-equity firm Mercato Partners (2007, with Alan Hall); his >10% MNTN stake comes via Mercato's early backing of SteelHouse, now ad-tech company MNTN. He also chaired the SPAC Mercato Partners Acquisition Corp and has sat on boards incl. Skullcandy, Fusion-io, Goal Zero and Domo.
interesting_fact: He holds a BS in Computer Science, an MBA and a PhD in Entrepreneurship and Venture Finance, all from the University of Utah's David Eccles School of Business.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Junto Partners, an education program that trains and mentors aspiring entrepreneurs, and has chaired the board of the Community Foundation of Utah.
notes: Active speaker/podcast guest in Utah startup scene. Mercato portfolio includes Goal Zero (portable solar power) - energy angle. Route via Mercato Partners.

name: David Phillips
current_role: Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer, Publix Super Markets; director since 2016
profile: David P. Phillips has spent his whole executive career at employee-owned Publix, joining in 1984 as an internal auditor after auditing the company for its outside accounting firm. He became controller in 1990, CFO in 1999 and EVP & CFO in 2016, and is a trustee of Publix's ESOP. His wealth comes from Publix stock (company is employee-owned, not listed).
interesting_fact: While auditing Publix for its outside auditors he decided the company was 'much better than other companies' and pursued a job there; he personally knew founder George Jenkins, whom he calls a 'complete genius'.
deep_cut_fact: A Lakeland, Florida native, after college he and his two brothers cycled across the U.S. from Astoria, Oregon to Yorktown, Virginia - about 2.5 months; he studied engineering and pre-med before switching to accounting.
notes: Lane data tags him 'Hurun Unicorn founders / Data Analytics' - likely a name collision; the SEC wealth is Publix CFO. Low public profile; route via Publix corporate communications. Jan 2025 media advisory names Jared Glover, Media Relations Manager (https://www.insidetheisle.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Publix-Media-Advisory-1.3.25.pdf).

name: Alesia J Haas
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Coinbase Global (since 2018); Director, Angi Inc.
profile: Alesia Haas became Coinbase's first CFO in April 2018 and steered the crypto exchange through its 2021 Nasdaq direct listing and later expansion. A former banker, she was previously CFO of Och-Ziff (Sculptor) Capital, CFO of OneWest Bank, and earlier at Merrill Lynch. She also sits on the board of Angi Inc.
interesting_fact: Fortune counts her among the '7 people with power at Coinbase', describing her as CEO Brian Armstrong's other top lieutenant who helped define what being a CFO means at a crypto firm.
deep_cut_fact: At OneWest Bank she was promoted from head of strategy to CFO in September 2012, and spent two years at Merrill Lynch Global Private Equity before that; she is a Cal Poly San Luis Obispo graduate.
notes: Cal Poly detail comes from secondary sources (IQ.wiki/Clay). Frequent speaker at fintech/CFO events (Fortune, Yahoo Finance interviews).

name: W. Sharps Robert
current_role: CEO, President and Chair of the Board, T. Rowe Price Group
profile: Robert W. (Rob) Sharps, CFA, joined T. Rowe Price in 1997 as a financial-services stock analyst, ran its Institutional Large-Cap Growth Equity strategy for 15 years, became head of investments/group CIO (2017-2021), president in 2021 and CEO in January 2022, later also chair.
interesting_fact: He started his career in 1993 as a senior management consultant at KPMG Peat Marwick and interned as an equity research analyst at Wellington Management before joining T. Rowe Price.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated summa cum laude in accounting from Towson University and serves on the boards of the Baltimore Curriculum Project and Bridges Baltimore, plus the Greater Washington Partnership.
notes: Name in source data is inverted ('W. Sharps Robert' = Robert W. Sharps). Baltimore-based; strong local civic profile.

name: Imran Ali Khan
current_role: Founder & Chair of Investment Committee, Proem Asset Management; co-founder of Verishop; director at Dave Inc. and Zeta Global
profile: Bangladeshi-American banker-turned-tech executive who led Credit Suisse's global internet banking (incl. a leading role on Alibaba's record IPO), then as Snap's Chief Strategy Officer (2015-2018) led its 2017 IPO. He co-founded social-commerce startup Verishop and founded hedge fund Proem Asset Management, whose 2023 stake brought him onto Dave's board.
interesting_fact: At JPMorgan he became one of the firm's youngest managing directors at 29, as head of global internet and U.S. entertainment equity research.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Dhaka, he was known as a strong debater at Dhaka College before moving to Colorado for university (University of Denver, 2000); his first job was at WildBlue, a Denver satellite-broadband startup.
notes: Spoke with Bangladesh Angels podcast about Verishop (https://bangladeshangels.substack.com/p/checking-in-with-imran-khan-ex-cso). Route via Proem Asset Management or Dave/Zeta corporate secretary; no published direct contact found.
